results.summary: Munch displays a munching squares animation on a VGA monitor while generating simple music through an audio PMOD. It uses the Tiny VGA and TT Audio pinouts and is implemented in Verilog. The author notes it works but requires a manual reset to sync the music properly. The design targets a 25.175 MHz input clock and was tested on fabricated silicon with partial success.

results.summary_before: This project is an alternative layout for Andrew Kang's mini-MOSbius, a reconfigurable analog array intended for building and experimenting with MOS circuits, adapted for SKY130 on Tiny Tapeout. It includes analog switches controlled by a serial bitstream, with digital logic for configuration, and it requires external hardware to generate the bitstream and to interface with the analog pins depending on the circuit being built. Silicon test reports indicate that the configuration shift registers work and that various circuits functioned properly. The design is notable for bringing the MOSbius educational concept to a Tiny Tapeout-compatible form, though the software suite for generating configuration bitstreams is not yet written.

results.summary_before: This design measures the frequency of an input signal by counting transitions over a configurable period and displays the result on a 7-segment display. It includes a debug mode that outputs internal signals on the bidirectional pins and allows the user to load a new count period via an input. The frequency is computed by repeatedly subtracting ten from the count and displaying the tens and units digits. The design requires a 10 MHz clock and external hardware such as a signal source and a 7-segment display.
